sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Some Microsoft services are not available in every country or region. Because of this, one property on a Microsoft Entra user account must be populated before a Microsoft 365 license can be assigned to that user. Which property must be set?
spiegazione: Correct: Usage location. The documentation states that because some Microsoft services aren't available in all locations, the administrator must specify the user's location setting before a license can be assigned to that user. Usage location is the attribute that licensing evaluates to determine which services may be enabled for the user. For group-based licensing, any users without a specific location inherit the location of the tenant. Incorrect - Office location: this is a descriptive profile/job attribute shown on the user's profile card; it has no effect on license assignment or service eligibility. Incorrect - Country or region: this is a contact/address attribute of the user profile. It is a common misconception that it drives licensing, but license assignment specifically evaluates Usage location, and the two are separate attributes that can hold different values. Incorrect - Preferred data location: this attribute is used with Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo to control the geography in which a user's data is stored at rest. It does not determine whether a license can be assigned.
tags: microsoft entra id,licensing,usage location,user properties,group-based licensing

domanda: A User Administrator at Fabrikam deletes the Microsoft Entra ID account of an employee who left the company. Two weeks later, HR reports that the employee is returning and the original account should be recovered with all of its properties. For how long after deletion does a user account remain in a suspended state where it can still be restored?
spiegazione: Correct: 30 days. The documentation states that after you delete a user, the account remains in a suspended state for 30 days, and during that 30-day window the user account can be restored along with all its properties. After the 30-day window passes, the permanent deletion process automatically starts and can't be stopped. Incorrect - 14 days: no 14-day soft-delete window exists for Microsoft Entra user accounts. Incorrect - 60 days: 60 days is not the Microsoft Entra soft-delete retention period. Incorrect - 90 days: 90 days is a retention value used by other Microsoft services (for example, certain sign-in and audit reporting retention scenarios), but it is not the deleted user restore window, which is fixed at 30 days.
tags: microsoft entra id,deleted users,restore,soft delete,30 days

domanda: An administrator needs to review which user accounts were recently deleted in Microsoft Entra ID and restore one of them from the Deleted users page in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Which is the least privileged built-in role that can perform this task?
spiegazione: Correct: User Administrator. The documented procedure for viewing restorable users and restoring a deleted user directs you to sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a User Administrator, then browse to Entra ID > Users > Deleted users. The same role is documented for permanently deleting a user and for bulk restore. Incorrect - Directory Readers: this role grants read access to basic directory information only; it cannot restore objects. Incorrect - Reports Reader: this role only reads sign-in and audit reporting data and usage reports; it has no user management permissions. Incorrect - Global Reader: Global Reader has broad read-only access across the tenant and can view deleted users, but read-only roles cannot perform the write operation of restoring an account. Restoring requires User Administrator.

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Contoso assigns a Microsoft 365 E3 license to a security group named GRP-All by using group-based licensing. GRP-All has 200 users as direct members and also contains a nested security group named GRP-Contractors, which has 40 users as members. None of the 40 contractors are direct members of GRP-All. Which users are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license?
opzione_a: Only the 200 direct members of GRP-All
opzione_b: All 240 users, because nested group membership is evaluated transitively
opzione_d: No users, because assigning a license to a group that contains a nested group is blocked
spiegazione: Correct: Only the 200 direct members of GRP-All. The documentation states that group-based licensing doesn't currently support nested groups, and that if you assign licenses to a nested group, only users in the first-level group are assigned licenses. The 40 contractors are members of the nested child group, not first-level members of GRP-All, so they receive nothing. Incorrect - All 240 users: this is the classic misconception. Transitive/nested evaluation is used by many Microsoft Entra features (for example, app assignment scenarios and some access checks), but group-based licensing explicitly does not process nested groups. Incorrect - Only the 40 members of GRP-Contractors: the license is assigned to GRP-All, and processing works downward to first-level members only; it is never restricted to the nested group alone. Incorrect - No users: the assignment is not blocked. It succeeds and licenses the first-level members; the nested members are simply ignored, which is why this limitation is easy to miss.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,nested groups,security group,limitations

domanda: An employee's account was deleted 10 days ago. At the time of deletion, the account had a Microsoft 365 E5 license assigned directly. Since then, the licenses have been consumed by new hires, and the tenant now shows zero available Microsoft 365 E5 licenses. An administrator restores the deleted account from the Deleted users page. What is the result?
opzione_a: The restore operation fails until an E5 license is freed or purchased.
opzione_b: The account is restored but with no licenses assigned, and the administrator must reassign a license manually.
opzione_c: The E5 license that was assigned at the time of deletion is restored with the account, and the organization can be temporarily out of compliance for license usage.
opzione_d: The account is restored and is automatically downgraded to a Microsoft Entra ID Free license until an E5 license becomes available.
spiegazione: Correct: The license is restored and the tenant can be temporarily out of compliance. The documentation explicitly notes that once a user is restored, licenses that were assigned to the user at the time of deletion are also restored even if there are none available, and that if you're consuming more licenses than you purchased, your organization could be temporarily out of compliance for license usage. Incorrect - The restore fails: license availability is not a gate on the restore operation; Microsoft Entra ID prioritizes returning the account to its previous state. Incorrect - Restored with no licenses: this contradicts the documented behavior. When a user account is deleted the account's organization information is preserved, and when you restore a user that information, including the license assignments, is restored. Incorrect - Automatically downgraded to Microsoft Entra ID Free: there is no automatic downgrade mechanism. The original assignment is reinstated as-is, which is precisely what creates the temporary compliance gap.

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Which Microsoft Graph PowerShell cmdlet returns the members of a group who failed to receive a license through group-based licensing, so that you can investigate the cause?
spiegazione: Correct: Get-MgGroupMemberWithLicenseError. This cmdlet is documented specifically for identifying the members of a group who are in an error state for group-based license assignment, which is the first step in troubleshooting problems such as insufficient licenses or conflicting service plans. Incorrect - Get-MgGroupMember: this returns all members of the group without any filtering on license assignment state, so it does not isolate the users in error. Incorrect - Get-MgSubscribedSku: this returns the subscribed SKUs in the tenant, including consumed and enabled unit counts. It is useful for checking how many licenses remain, but it reports at the tenant/SKU level and does not identify which group members failed. Incorrect - Set-MgGroupLicense: this is a write cmdlet used to add or remove license assignments on a group; it configures group-based licensing rather than reporting errors.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,microsoft graph powershell,troubleshooting,license errors

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: At Litware, a user account is synchronized from Windows Server Active Directory to Microsoft Entra ID by using Microsoft Entra Connect. Group-based license assignment for the user fails because the Usage location property is empty. The on-premises identity team confirms that the user's identity, contact, and job attributes must be changed on-premises. You must populate Usage location for the user with the least administrative effort. What should you do?
opzione_a: Set the Usage location property on the user directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
opzione_b: Populate the country attribute on the user object in Windows Server Active Directory and wait for the next synchronization cycle.
opzione_c: Create a custom inbound synchronization rule in Microsoft Entra Connect that maps an on-premises attribute to usageLocation.
opzione_d: Exclude the user's organizational unit from synchronization so that the account becomes cloud-only, and then set Usage location.
spiegazione: Correct: Set Usage location directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center. The documentation states that for users whose source of authority is Windows Server Active Directory you must use Windows Server Active Directory to update their identity, contact info, or job info; however, you can update their attributes directly in the Microsoft Entra admin center if you are updating Microsoft Entra ID attributes, such as Usage Location. Usage location is a Microsoft Entra ID attribute, so the on-premises source-of-authority restriction does not apply to it. Incorrect - Populate the country attribute on-premises: usageLocation is not synchronized from the on-premises country attribute by default, so this would not resolve the failure, and it also changes an attribute users may see. Incorrect - Create a custom synchronization rule: this can work but is far more administrative effort than editing an attribute that Microsoft Entra ID already allows you to edit directly, and custom sync rules add ongoing maintenance and upgrade risk. Incorrect - Exclude the OU to make the account cloud-only: this is a drastic change that breaks the hybrid identity model for that user and is unnecessary, since the attribute is directly editable in the cloud.
tags: microsoft entra id,usage location,microsoft entra connect,hybrid identity,user properties,licensing

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Adventure Works uses group-based licensing. A Microsoft 365 E3 license is assigned to the group GRP-Sales and also to the group GRP-Marketing. Several users are transferring from Sales to Marketing. You must move the users between the two groups so that they do not lose access to licensed services at any point during the move. What should you do?
opzione_a: Remove the users from GRP-Sales, and then add them to GRP-Marketing.
opzione_b: Add the users to GRP-Marketing, confirm that the new license has been applied on each user's Licenses page, and then remove them from GRP-Sales.
opzione_c: Remove the users from GRP-Sales and add them to GRP-Marketing within the same bulk membership operation.
opzione_d: Assign a Microsoft 365 E3 license directly to each user, remove them from GRP-Sales, and then add them to GRP-Marketing.
spiegazione: Correct: Add to the destination group first, confirm the license applied, then remove from the source group. The documentation states that when you move a user from one licensed group to another the order of operations matters, and prescribes exactly this sequence to move a user between licensed groups without service interruption. Incorrect - Remove first, then add: this is the documented failure mode. If you remove the user from the source group first, the user is unlicensed until group-based licensing finishes processing the new group's assignment, and processing time varies by tenant size and load. Incorrect - Same bulk operation: bundling both changes into one operation does not guarantee ordering or immediate processing. Group-based licensing processes membership changes asynchronously, so the user can still be left temporarily unlicensed. Incorrect - Assign a direct license first: this does technically mask the gap, but it is not the documented approach and it creates a direct license assignment on every user that must later be cleaned up, defeating the purpose of group-based licensing and risking double consumption.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,group membership,service interruption,license processing

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: You are delegating permissions at Northwind Traders so that helpdesk staff can assign product licenses to groups in the Microsoft 365 admin center, without granting Global Administrator. Which built-in roles allow a user to assign licenses to a group? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
spiegazione: Correct: Groups Administrator, License Administrator, and User Administrator. The documentation states that you must be at least a Groups Administrator, License Administrator, or User Administrator to assign licenses to a group. Incorrect - Billing Administrator: this role manages purchases, subscriptions, invoices and payment methods. It can buy licenses for the tenant, but purchasing licenses is not the same as assigning them to users or groups, which is the classic confusion this option tests. Incorrect - Helpdesk Administrator: this role is scoped to resetting passwords and managing sign-in and service requests for non-administrator users. It is not among the roles documented for license assignment.

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: After assigning a product license to a group, an administrator opens the product details page in the Microsoft 365 admin center and reviews the Errors & issues tab, which lists members who have license assignment problems. Which of the following are documented causes of group license assignment errors? Select all that apply. Each correct answer presents part of the solution.
opzione_a: There are not enough available licenses in the subscription for every member of the group.
opzione_b: The assignment includes service plans that conflict and cannot be assigned to the same user.
opzione_c: Two members of the group have duplicate proxy addresses.
opzione_d: The group contains a nested group whose members push the total membership above the purchased license count.
opzione_e: One of the group members has a disabled sign-in status.
spiegazione: Correct: insufficient licenses, conflicting service plans, and duplicate proxy addresses. The documentation lists the group license error types as insufficient licenses, conflicting service plans, missing dependencies, proxy address issues, and usage location problems. Insufficient licenses occurs when the subscription does not have enough units for every member; conflicting service plans occurs when two service plans in the assignment cannot coexist on the same user; proxy address issues occur when more than one object carries the same proxy address, which blocks the Exchange-related service plan. Incorrect - Nested group members pushing membership above the license count: nested group members are never processed by group-based licensing at all, since only first-level members are assigned licenses. They therefore cannot consume licenses or generate this error. Incorrect - A member with a disabled sign-in status: account enablement is unrelated to license assignment. Disabled accounts can still hold licenses and do not appear as a license assignment error.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,license conflicts,service plans,proxy address,troubleshooting

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Woodgrove Bank manages product licenses for thousands of users by using group-based licensing in the Microsoft 365 admin center. An administrator is planning a bulk assignment and needs to account for the documented limitations of the feature. Select the correct value for each statement.
opzione_a: Maximum number of groups you can assign licenses to at a time: [10 | 20 | 50]
opzione_b: Maximum number of users the Reprocess action attempts to reprocess at a time: [20 | 100 | 999]
opzione_c: Number of users displayed at a time in the paginated lists of successful and unsuccessful assignments: [100 | 500 | 999]
spiegazione: Correct values are 20, 20, and 999. The documented limitations of group-based licensing in the Microsoft 365 admin center state that you can assign licenses to a maximum of 20 groups at a time; that when you select Reprocess to resolve issues with group license assignment, the feature attempts to reprocess licenses up to a maximum of 20 users at a time; and that the lists of users who were and who weren't successfully assigned licenses are paginated lists that display 999 users at a time, requiring you to scroll to the bottom to load the next set. Incorrect - 10 or 50 groups: these are plausible-looking round numbers but the documented ceiling is 20 groups per assignment operation. Incorrect - 100 or 999 users for Reprocess: Reprocess is capped at 20 users per action, not 999; 999 is the pagination size of the result lists, which is the value this distractor deliberately confuses it with. Incorrect - 100 or 500 users per page: the documented pagination size is 999.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,limits,reprocess,microsoft 365 admin center

domanda: Tailspin Toys is documenting its recovery procedures for accidentally deleted Microsoft Entra ID objects. Select the correct value to complete each statement.
opzione_a: Period during which a deleted user account remains in a suspended state and can be restored: [14 days | 30 days | 90 days]
opzione_b: Group types that can be restored after deletion: [Distribution groups only | Microsoft 365 groups and cloud security groups | All group types, including distribution groups]
opzione_c: The group restoration period can be customized: [Yes | No]
risposta_corretta: 30 days,Microsoft 365 groups and cloud security groups,No
spiegazione: Correct values are 30 days, Microsoft 365 groups and cloud security groups, and No. For users, the documentation states that after you delete a user the account remains in a suspended state for 30 days and can be restored during that window. For groups, the documentation states that restore functionality is available for Microsoft 365 groups and cloud security groups in Microsoft Entra ID, that it isn't available for distribution groups, that the deleted group is retained but not visible for 30 days from the deletion date, and that the 30-day group restoration period isn't customizable. Incorrect - 14 days or 90 days: the user soft-delete window is fixed at 30 days. Incorrect - Distribution groups only: this is the inverse of the truth, since distribution groups are precisely the type excluded from restore. Incorrect - All group types including distribution groups: distribution groups are explicitly not supported. Incorrect - Yes for customization: the retention period is fixed by the service and cannot be changed by an administrator.
tags: microsoft entra id,restore,deleted groups,deleted users,soft delete,retention

sotto_argomento: Manage licenses in Microsoft Entra ID
domanda: Proseware uses group-based licensing. A Microsoft 365 E3 product license is assigned to a security group named GRP-Engineering. GRP-Engineering contains 500 direct user members and one nested security group named GRP-Interns that contains 25 users who are not direct members of GRP-Engineering. All users have a Usage location configured. Evaluate each of the following statements and indicate whether it is true. 1) When a new user is added as a direct member of GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID automatically assigns the Microsoft 365 E3 license to that user. 2) When a user is removed from GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID removes the license assignment that the user inherited from the group. 3) The 25 users in GRP-Interns are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license because their group is a member of GRP-Engineering.
opzione_a: When a new user is added as a direct member of GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID automatically assigns the Microsoft 365 E3 license to that user.
opzione_b: When a user is removed from GRP-Engineering, Microsoft Entra ID removes the license assignment that the user inherited from the group.
opzione_c: The 25 users in GRP-Interns are assigned the Microsoft 365 E3 license because their group is a member of GRP-Engineering.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: the documentation states that Microsoft Entra users who join a licensed group are automatically assigned the appropriate licenses, which is the core value of group-based licensing and removes the need for scripts to license joiners. Statement 2 - Yes: the documentation states that when users leave the group, Microsoft Entra ID removes their license assignments. Note this only reclaims the license inherited from the group; a license that was also assigned directly to the user would remain and must be removed separately. Statement 3 - No: group-based licensing doesn't currently support nested groups. If you assign licenses to a group, only users in the first-level group are assigned licenses, so the 25 members of the nested GRP-Interns receive nothing and would need to be direct members of GRP-Engineering, or have the license assigned to GRP-Interns itself.
tags: microsoft entra id,group-based licensing,nested groups,license inheritance,group membership

domanda: Relecloud has a hybrid identity environment. User1 is a cloud-only account that was deleted 20 days ago. User2 was synchronized from Windows Server Active Directory by using Microsoft Entra Connect, was deleted in Microsoft Entra ID for security reasons, and still exists in the on-premises directory. User3 was deleted 45 days ago and has already been permanently removed. Evaluate each of the following statements and indicate whether it is true. 1) User1 can be restored from the Deleted users page in the Microsoft Entra admin center. 2) Microsoft Support can restore User3 on request. 3) The synchronization engine may restore User2 during the next synchronization cycle.
opzione_a: User1 can be restored from the Deleted users page in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
opzione_b: Microsoft Support can restore User3 on request.
opzione_c: The synchronization engine may restore User2 during the next synchronization cycle.
spiegazione: Statement 1 - Yes: User1 was deleted 20 days ago, which is inside the 30-day window. The documentation states you can see all the users that were deleted less than 30 days ago and that these users can be restored, along with all their properties. Statement 2 - No: User3 was deleted 45 days ago, so the automatic permanent deletion process has already run. The documentation is explicit that after the 30-day window passes the permanent deletion process automatically starts and can't be stopped, and that after a user is permanently deleted, neither you nor Microsoft Support can restore them. The only remedy is to create a new user and manually re-enter the information. Statement 3 - Yes: the documentation notes that although you can delete synced users in Microsoft Entra ID for security purposes, Microsoft Entra ID isn't the source of authority for synced users, and if the user still exists in your on-premises directory the sync engine may restore the user during the next synchronization cycle. To remove such a user durably, the account must be handled in the on-premises directory.
tags: microsoft entra id,restore deleted users,permanent deletion,hybrid identity,microsoft entra connect,source of authority

domanda: A misconfigured offboarding script at Fourth Coffee deleted 120 Microsoft Entra ID user accounts yesterday. You sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as a User Administrator and browse to Entra ID > Users > Deleted users. You must restore all 120 accounts in a single operation by using bulk restore. Arrange the following actions in the correct order.
opzione_a: Browse to the completed CSV file and select Submit to start validation of the file.
opzione_b: Review the outcome of the job on the Bulk operation results page.
opzione_c: On the Deleted users page, select Bulk restore.
opzione_d: Download the CSV template and add a row containing the Object ID of each user to restore.
opzione_e: After the file passes validation, select Submit to start the bulk restore operation.
spiegazione: The documented bulk restore sequence is: (1) On the Deleted users page, select Bulk restore to upload a valid CSV file of properties of the users to restore. (2) Open the CSV template and add a line for each user you want to restore; the only required value is ObjectID, and the version row and column header row must be kept exactly as downloaded or the upload can't be processed. (3) Under Upload your csv file, browse to the file and select Submit, which starts validation of the CSV file. (4) When the file contents are validated you see File uploaded successfully; if there are errors you must fix them before you can submit the job. When your file passes validation, select Submit to start the bulk operation that restores the users. (5) You can see the status of all of your pending bulk requests on the Bulk operation results page, and if you experience errors you can download the results file, which contains the reason for each error. The most common ordering mistake is attempting to upload before selecting Bulk restore, or treating the first Submit (validation) as the action that performs the restore; validation and execution are two distinct Submit steps.
tags: microsoft entra id,bulk restore,deleted users,csv,bulk operations
